raw.body:
I dug through the 19.2 path a bit more. I don't think the safest backport is just an `alreadyFlushed` check inside `flushCompletedBoundary`, because by that point the same boundary has already been queued twice and a late fallback may also have re-assigned the root segment id. A guard there could also get tricky with backpressure, since a boundary may need to resume a partially completed flush.

The better fix seems to be preventing the stale fallback segment from re-entering/serializing an already revealed content boundary in the first place.

This looks related to #33467 (`[Fizz] Support deeply nested Suspense inside fallback`). That change specifically handles completed/aborted segments inside fallbacks that are no longer observable and preserves the root-segment invariant. I haven't confirmed yet whether that exact commit is what makes the January 2026 canaries pass, but it would be the first commit I'd test for a 19.2 backport.

I think the regression test should cover at least:

* outlined content completes before a root-suspending fallback
* the same case with and without destination backpressure
* fallback completes first as the control case
* content below/above the outlining threshold
* fallback suspending through a nested child, not only an `async` fallback component
* a late fallback error/abort
* nested fallback Suspense and SuspenseList bookkeeping

The important assertion should be one reveal per logical boundary, rather than only checking duplicate ids, since the failing path can re-declare the same boundary with a new `B:*`/`S:*` pair.

I'm happy to put together a focused regression test / try the relevant backport if maintainers can confirm that #33467 is the intended main-branch fix.
